preExistingTestDefectFound.claim: The original code did NOT actually use two separate databases, despite naming variables DB_FILE and DB_FILE2 and unlinking each separately.
evidence: DB_FILE = path.join(DATA_DIR, 'pos.db') where DATA_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'data') -> resolves to ROOT/data/pos.db (the REAL production database).
DB_FILE2 = path.join(ROOT, 'data/pos.db') -> resolves to the IDENTICAL path, ROOT/data/pos.db. Not a different file at all.

Both section O and section P did `const { initDb, getDb } = require(path.join(ROOT, 'utils/db.js'))` -- the exact same resolved absolute path both times, with ZERO require.cache eviction anywhere in the file (confirmed by grep).

utils/db.js's initDb() has an internal guard `if (wrappedDb) return wrappedDb;` -- so section P's initDb() call did not create a new in-memory database; it returned the SAME already-created wrappedDb object from section O.

Consequence: section P's `db2` was literally the same JS object reference as section O's `db`. Deleting the real data/pos.db FILE on disk between sections had no effect on this already-loaded in-memory object -- section O's fixture data (store_a12, store_a12_other, and their geo visit logs) remained present in memory when section P ran.
preExistingTestDefectFound.whyAssertionsStillPassedDespiteTheDefect: Section P's assertions all query specifically for 'store_partial' (a store_id never used in section O), so the leftover section-O data in the shared in-memory object never became visible to section P's queries. This was accidental correctness from store_id-based filtering, not real isolation by design.
preExistingTestDefectFound.fixApplied: Section P now: computes a genuinely separate sibling temp DB path via dbHelper.createChildDbPath(dbContext.tmpRoot, 'db2'); sets POS_DB_PATH to it (full replacement, never unset/emptied); evicts require.cache ONLY for utils/db.js's own resolved absolute path (confirmed safe -- see moduleCacheEvictionAudit below); re-requires utils/db.js, producing a genuinely fresh module instance with its own independent wrappedDb. Section O and section P now use two REAL, independent, isolated temp databases, matching the code's apparent original intent.
preExistingTestDefectFound.assertionBehaviorUnchanged: Confirmed via the AST full-argument comparison above (212/212 identical) -- fixing the underlying defect required zero changes to any assertion condition, since none of them depend on DB1/DB2 sharing or not sharing state (section P always filters by the disjoint store_partial store_id).

selfProvingAssertions.bugFoundDuringImplementation: Initial Q1/Q2b design used fs.realpathSync(db2Path), which would have thrown ENOENT: DB2's underlying file does not exist on disk at that point in execution, because utils/db.js's initTables() (called inside initDb()) uses the RAW sql.js .run() method, not the save()-triggering wrapped one -- nothing is persisted to disk until the first real data-modifying write. Fixed by using path.resolve() (pure string resolution) for db2Path instead of realpathSync, while still using realpathSync for db1RealPath and the temp root (both guaranteed to exist by that point: DB1's file was already written via section O's INSERT statements, and the temp root is created synchronously by mkdtempSync during bootstrap).
selfProvingAssertions.secondBugFoundDuringImplementation: The initial edit declared `const dbModule1 = require(...)` inside section O's own block scope, then referenced `dbModule1` from section P's separate block in the new Q3 assertion -- a genuine block-scoping error that would have thrown ReferenceError at runtime. Caught by manually re-reading the full modified code end-to-end (node --check does not catch this class of error, since it is a valid parse, only an invalid runtime reference). Fixed by hoisting `dbModule1`/`db` to main()-function scope (declared with `let` immediately before section O's block) so both section O and section P/Q can reference them.

utilsDbJsSourceCitations.consequenceIfMigrationsThrow: wrappedDb is already a truthy, partially-initialized object by the time initTables() could throw. getDb() (line 76-79) only checks truthiness, so it would happily return this partial handle -- but the caller's own `await initDb()` promise has already rejected, so a caller who only calls getDb() AFTER a successful initDb() (as this file does) would never reach that getDb() call and would never learn about or register this partially-initialized handle.
utilsDbJsSourceCitations.failedModuleGenerationCacheStatus: require.cache is NOT automatically cleared on a thrown initDb() -- the module instance (and its now-partially-initialized wrappedDb) remains cached under its resolved absolute path unless explicitly evicted, which this file does not do after a failure (only proactively before DB2's intentional fresh generation).

initFailureHandleSafety.fixApplied: initDbSafely(dbModule) wrapper: on success, registers the handle immediately after getDb() (before any subsequent operation that could throw). On initDb() failure, makes a best-effort attempt to retrieve whatever partial handle exists via getDb() (wrapped in its own try/catch so a further getDb() failure -- meaning wrappedDb was never assigned at all, e.g. initSqlJs() itself failed before line 84 -- does not mask anything), registers it if found, then ALWAYS rethrows the ORIGINAL initDb() error, never the best-effort retrieval's own error.
initFailureHandleSafety.handleRegistrationTiming: immediately after getDb() returns (success path) or immediately after the best-effort getDb() retrieval (failure path) -- in both cases, before any subsequent db.run()/other operation that could throw
initFailureHandleSafety.failedGenerationNeverReusedAsSuccessful: each of the two initDbSafely() calls operates on its own freshly-required module instance (dbModule1, dbModule2) -- there is no retry-without-cache-eviction logic anywhere in this file that could accidentally reuse a failed generation as if it had succeeded
initFailureHandleSafety.staticVsRuntimeProvenClarification: This entire initDbSafely() analysis is verificationMethod: staticSourceAudit throughout -- no failure injection was actually run against the dual-DB child (which remains unexecuted per the Batch C child execution prohibition). No claim of runtimeProven is made anywhere in this evidence file for the dual-DB child itself. Separately, the SHARED helper functions (dbHelper.runCleanupSteps/runCleanupStepsAsync/handleOwnedCleanup) DO have real, executed, runtime-proven failure-injection tests (CLEANUP-POLICY1-4, ASYNC-CLEANUP-POLICY1-7, etc. in scripts/run-h1-4-8-product-funnel-semantics-runtime.js) -- but those tests exercise the shared helper directly with synthetic dbContext objects, not this specific file's initDbSafely() wrapper or its two real utils/db.js call sites.

containmentCheckCorrection.problem: The prior turn's Q1(old)/Q2b(old) used path.resolve(db2Path) for BOTH the distinctness check AND as if it were a containment proof -- path.resolve() is pure string resolution and proves nothing about actual filesystem location/escape safety.
containmentCheckCorrection.fix: Split into two explicitly separate, differently-named checks: distinctPathCheck (Q1, path.resolve-based, only proves DB1 != DB2 as paths, explicitly labeled as NOT a containment proof) and containmentCheck (Q2 for DB1, Q3 for DB2, both using fs.realpathSync() on the PARENT DIRECTORY -- which is guaranteed to exist even before the DB file itself is persisted, since createChildDbPath() places files directly inside dbContext.tmpRoot, never a not-yet-created subdirectory -- combined with path.relative(rootReal, parentReal) and explicit escape-pattern checks: rel !== "..", !rel.startsWith(".." + path.sep), !path.isAbsolute(rel). This mirrors the exact escape-detection method already used in scripts/lib/qa-temp-db.js's validateParentProvidedDb(), not a new/different method.
containmentCheckCorrection.supplementaryFileLevelCheck: Q10 added: AFTER section P's writes guarantee the DB2 file is actually persisted to disk (db2.run() triggers the wrapped save()), a supplementary FILE-level (not just parent-directory-level) realpath containment check is performed. Before that point, a file-level check would have either thrown ENOENT or required fabricating a result for a non-existent file -- neither acceptable, so it is correctly deferred to when it can be genuinely performed, not skipped or faked.
containmentCheckCorrection.filenameArgvEnvIndependence: DB2's filename itself is generated entirely inside createChildDbPath() via `${safeLabel}-${crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex')}.db` -- the label this file passes in is the fixed literal string 'db2' (not from argv/env), and the random suffix is generated by the helper itself, not by this file or any external input.

correctionsThisTurn.originalContainmentCheckWasNotFullyWrong: The Q1(old) distinctness comparison itself (db1RealPath !== db2ResolvedPath) was a valid distinctness check, just mislabeled/conflated with containment in the surrounding commentary.
